# Figures, Tables, and Apps {.unnumbered}

A consolidated index of every numbered figure and table in the book, plus the interactive Shiny apps. Click any entry to jump to it in context.

## Interactive apps

* @sec-nr-divergence-app (in *Optimization for Maximum Likelihood Estimation*) — choose a starting value for Newton-Raphson on a logistic log-likelihood and step through the iterations, watching the method converge or run away.
* @sec-mixture-app (in *EM Algorithms*) — run the EM algorithm on a two-component normal mixture from a chosen starting point and step through the E- and M-steps.
* @sec-bayes-explorer (in *Introduction to Bayesian Inference*) — pick a conjugate model and its prior, generate data, and watch the posterior update.
* @sec-missed-mode (in *Numerical Quadrature*) — move a Gaussian posterior's mode and see the fixed midpoint grid miss it entirely.
* @sec-laplace-transform-app (in *Laplace Approximation*) — compare the Laplace approximation against adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature and Monte Carlo as a posterior's shape changes.
* @sec-rejection-app (in *Rejection Sampling*) — tune the tightness of a Laplace envelope around a standard normal target and watch the acceptance rate respond.
* @sec-gamma-rejection-app (in *Rejection Sampling*) — tune a Cauchy envelope against a Gamma target and see acceptance collapse as the shape parameter moves away from the tuned point.
* @sec-ars-app (in *Rejection Sampling*) — watch adaptive rejection sampling build and refine its piecewise-linear hull around a log-concave density.
* @sec-importance-app (in *Importance Sampling*) — move a normal proposal relative to a mixture target and watch the effective sample size and estimate quality respond.
* @sec-hmc-app (in *Markov Chain Monte Carlo*) — tune the step size and number of leapfrog steps of Hamiltonian Monte Carlo on a correlated target and compare against random-walk Metropolis.

## Figures

### Introduction to Statistical Computation

* @fig-sampling-distributions — two sampling distributions for the same target, contrasting bias and variance.
* @fig-null-alternative-distributions — null and alternative distributions of a test statistic, with type I error, power, and the p-value shown as tail areas.
* @fig-intro-prior-likelihood-posterior — a vague prior, the likelihood, and the resulting posterior for a normal mean.
* @fig-uniform-sum-hist — simulated distribution of the sum of two independent uniforms, approximating the true triangular density.
* @fig-gamma-maximizer — a Gamma density whose maximizer is obvious by eye, contrasted with harder optimization problems.
* @fig-quadrature-rectangles — numerical quadrature by the rectangle rule, approximating the area under a Gamma density.

### Introduction to R and Quarto

* @fig-course-score-hist — distribution of simulated course scores across the class.
* @fig-course-score-by-program — course score by academic program, with individual scores jittered over boxplots.
* @fig-final-vs-quiz-by-program — final exam score versus mean quiz score, by program, revealing a built-in intercept offset.

### Computer Arithmetic

* @fig-toy-lines — positive numbers at two zoom levels on a toy decimal computer, showing where marks crowd and where overflow occurs.

### Random Number Generator and Monte Carlo Elements

* @fig-lcg-vs-runif — a hand-rolled linear congruential generator versus R's built-in `runif()`.
* @fig-inverse-cdf-exp — exponential samples generated by the inverse-CDF method, compared with `rexp()`.
* @fig-box-muller — normal samples generated by the Box-Muller transform, compared with `rnorm()`.
* @fig-lln-clt-gamma — the Law of Large Numbers and Central Limit Theorem illustrated with Gamma draws.
* @fig-mc-pi-darts — Monte Carlo estimation of $\pi$ by throwing darts at a square.

### Point Estimation and Hypothesis Testing

* @fig-prop-mse-plot — simulated MSE of the MLE versus a smoothed estimator of a binomial proportion, across sample sizes.
* @fig-t-test-df100 — null distribution of t-test p-values at df = 100: uniform, as expected.
* @fig-t-test-df3 — null distribution of t-test p-values at df = 3: heavy tails distort the p-value distribution.
* @fig-t-test-df1 — null distribution of t-test p-values at df = 1 (Cauchy): the test breaks down completely.
* @fig-t-test-n30 — null distribution of t-test p-values at $n=30$: the CLT restores uniformity.
* @fig-t-test-power-df5 — power of the t-test at df = 5 against a true mean shift.
* @fig-t-test-power-df3 — power of the t-test at df = 3 against a true mean shift.
* @fig-perm-cor-illustration — permutation distribution of the absolute correlation for non-normal, dependent data.
* @fig-perm-cor-normal-h0 — null distribution of the permutation-test p-value for correlation, normal data.
* @fig-perm-cor-nonnormal-h0 — permutation test versus Pearson test under the null, independent non-normal data.
* @fig-test-lm-sel-h0 — the false-positive cascade from naively selecting the best-correlated of 20 predictors.
* @fig-perm-lm-sel-size-power — the permutation fix restoring valid size after variable selection.
* @fig-power-regression-h0 — naive versus permutation-corrected p-values for the best power transformation of $X$.
* @fig-power-regression-power — power of the permutation test to detect two non-linear signals.

### Optimization for Maximum Likelihood Estimation

* @fig-normal-loglik-score-curvature — log-likelihood, score, and curvature for a normal mean at two sample sizes.
* @fig-cauchy-loglik-by-n — Cauchy log-likelihood sharpening around the truth as sample size grows.
* @fig-cauchy-loglik-variability — repeated Cauchy log-likelihood curves clustering more tightly as $n$ grows.
* @fig-scheme-fixed-point — fixed-point iteration as a cobweb diagram.
* @fig-scheme-bisection — bisection on the score function, halving the bracket at each step.
* @fig-scheme-newton — Newton-Raphson following the tangent to the score, contrasted with a Fisher-scoring step.
* @fig-cauchy-single-obs — single-observation Cauchy likelihood whose flat tails defeat Newton-Raphson.
* @fig-scheme-golden — golden section search reusing one interior point per iteration.
* @fig-golden-tests — golden section search on a smooth log-likelihood and on a non-differentiable function.
* @fig-nzp-loglik-score — log-likelihood and score for the zero-truncated Poisson model.
* @fig-nzp-convergence-plot — error decay of simple iteration, Newton-Raphson, and scoring for the zero-truncated Poisson MLE.
* @fig-nzp-quadratic-approx — zero-truncated Poisson log-likelihood versus its quadratic approximation at the MLE.
* @fig-nzp-mle-vs-naive — sampling distributions of the naive estimator versus the MLE for a zero-truncated Poisson mean.
* @fig-interval-poisson-loglik — log-likelihood for an interval-censored Poisson mean under narrow versus wide censoring.
* @fig-logistic-data — simulated logistic regression data with the true success probability curve.

### EM Algorithms

* @fig-q-average — complete-data log-likelihood curves, their average, and the exact $Q$ function.
* @fig-tangent-bound — three EM iterations viewed as successive tangent minorants of the observed log-likelihood.
* @fig-mixture-components — the observed mixture density as a sum of two weighted normal components.
* @fig-mixture-shapes — how separation and mixing proportion determine whether a mixture is visibly bimodal.
* @fig-estep — the E-step responsibility as a share of density at a point, and as a function of $y$.
* @fig-mix-data — simulated mixture data, coloured by the normally unobserved component label.
* @fig-truncation — a density split at a cut point, and the two renormalized conditional densities.
* @fig-poisson-estep — the conditional distribution of a censored count under the Poisson E-step.
* @fig-clustering — a three-component multivariate normal mixture with unequal covariances.
* @fig-hmm — a two-state hidden Markov chain with normal emissions and shaded hidden states.

### Introduction to Bayesian Inference

* @fig-prior-likelihood-posterior — a diffuse prior and a concentrated likelihood combining into a posterior close to the likelihood.
* @fig-predictive — the posterior predictive density as an average over the sampling densities at posterior draws.
* @fig-beta-priors — six Beta priors spanning flat, U-shaped, and concentrated shapes.
* @fig-beta-posterior-narrowing — a Beta posterior narrowing and moving onto the MLE as $n$ grows.
* @fig-pg-predictive-dispersion — Negative-Binomial posterior predictive against a plug-in Poisson, showing extra dispersion.
* @fig-nn-predictive-dispersion — normal posterior predictive against a plug-in normal, showing the extra predictive spread.

### Numerical Quadrature

* @fig-logistic-transform — the logistic transform mapping equally spaced points to unequally spaced ones without changing the integral.
* @fig-convergence — convergence rates of midpoint, trapezoid, and Simpson's rule as the panel count grows.
* @fig-prior-sensitivity — one likelihood combined with three priors, with the marginal likelihood as a shaded area.
* @fig-grid — a two-parameter posterior on its natural scale and after transformation to the unit square, with the midpoint grid overlaid.
* @fig-curse — a correlated 2-D posterior's negligible-mass region, and how grid evaluations explode with dimension.

### Laplace Approximation

* @fig-poisson-gamma-density — the exact Gamma posterior versus its Laplace normal approximation, at two sample sizes.

### Rejection Sampling

* @fig-envelope-scatter — a normal target under its Laplace envelope, with accepted candidate points shown.
* @fig-gamma-tests — Q-Q plots of rejection-sampled Gamma draws against the true distribution.
* @fig-ars — histograms of adaptive-rejection-sampled draws against the true truncated normal density.

### Importance Sampling

* @fig-missed-mode — a proposal that misses a mode of the target, with weights that look deceptively healthy.

### Markov Chain Monte Carlo

* @fig-two-walks — long-run state frequencies for a cyclic random walk versus a reflecting one.
* @fig-gibbs-demo — Gibbs sampler trace plots and posterior densities for a normal mean and variance.
* @fig-tnorm-mh — random-walk Metropolis targeting a truncated normal, at three step sizes.
* @fig-stepsize — trace and autocorrelation for a random-walk sampler with step size too small, about right, and too large.
* @fig-mh-stepsize-search — preliminary Metropolis-Hastings runs at four step-size scales.
* @fig-hmc-vs-rw — Hamiltonian Monte Carlo versus random-walk Metropolis on a correlated target.
* @fig-stan-sv — simulated stochastic-volatility data and Stan's posterior for the model's top-level parameters.
